cleared.check: Task 1 (L-1222). Every MUL, DIV, MOD and MULMOD instruction of the 128 un-entered value blocks, 33 sites in blocks 0x28f2, 0x2907, 0x4f43, 0x51cf, 0x56cb, 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a, 0x58db and 0x5d71: 16 non-literal MUL, 2 MUL with a literal operand, 6 non-literal DIV, 2 DIV with the literal 1,000,000, 1 MOD, and 6 MULMOD (modulus 2^128 at 0x576a and 2^96 at 0x586f, both inline; the all-ones modulus at 0x58c1; 1,000,000 at 0x57f1; a run-time modulus at 0x51de and 0x58eb). The cycle 31 hook state before each site (research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/out/states.jsonl) was laid out as the gcc 15.2.0 build reads the Stack, including the deferred comparison at 0x5d78 (Stack+0x128 and +0x130 hold raw StackElem pointers, +0x138 the Comparison, read from Stack::discharge_deferred_comparison 0x3ac3b0). The package's whole Emitter::mul(long) 0x3838e0, udiv(long) 0x383a20, umod(long) 0x387840 or mulmod(long) 0x387590 then ran in the cycle 27 x86 model with its whole direct-call closure from the package text (137 functions, out/closure.txt: mul_optimized, div_optimized<false>, mod_optimized<false>, modop_optimized<mulmod> with mul_mod2, MulEmitter, call_runtime_impl, spill_all_caller_save_general_regs, spill_avx_reg_range, RuntimeImpl::pass, mov_arg with its jump table, RuntimeImpl::call_impl, Stack::pop, push and alloc_stack_offset, the allocators). Only asmjit _emitI, RoData::add4, add8 and add32, operator new and delete, memcpy, memset and the libstdc++ tree routines are stubs. Every asmjit call was recorded. The model gained vshufps (VEX.128, used by MulEmitter::mul_sequence<false> at 0x3a1a92) and indirect jmp and call through a register or memory operand.
cleared.result: All 33 gcc streams equal the clang listing body at the same pc up to consistent renaming. At 0x5934 the clang listing uses limb orders r10, r11, r8, r9 and rdi, rcx, rsi, rdx for the second and third register rows, which earlier blocks leave behind and the hook log does not carry; with that table read from the listing's stores the gcc stream is equal. At all 33 sites the gcc Stack after the call equals the clang hook state before the next instruction in every element location, available offset, free register queue, delta and deferred comparison. 66,000 runs of the gcc streams (2,000 per site, seed 3232, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and SwapMath shaped words, denominators and moduli with a top limb of 0, 1 and all ones, edge words) gave no wrong result and no overwritten live word against pyevm.py (research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/realarith.json). The runtime calls in these runs executed the package's own helper text, so the helpers' real register and memory clobbers acted on the live state.

cleared.check: Task 2. At each of the 30 runtime calls the gcc streams make (the two power-of-two MULMOD sites and the literal MUL at 0x58f9 emit no call): which registers carry the arguments and the result pointer, what is saved before the call, whether vector registers survive it, whether the stack is aligned, and whether the result pointer may alias an argument (research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/task2.json).
cleared.result: Every call is lea rsi, lea rdx (and lea rcx for MULMOD) to the operand slots [rbp+32k] or to RoData constants, lea rdi to the result slot that Stack::alloc_stack_offset returned, then call qword ptr [ROD+k] whose 8-byte constant is the helper address (0x44e160 monad_vm_runtime_mul, 0x397250 runtime::udiv, 0x397710 runtime::umod, 0x398a70 runtime::mulmod). Stack::spill_all_caller_save_general_regs stores the r8 to r11 and rcx, rsi, rdx, rdi rows of every live element before the call; after the emit only the callee-saved r12 to r15 row holds live words in general registers. udiv, umod and mulmod pass spill_avx 1 (bytes at 0x383a9e, 0x3878be, 0x38760e), spill every AVX register and emit vzeroupper; mul passes 0 (0x38395e) and keeps live AVX words in ymm across the call (0x56dd keeps ymm0 and ymm1), which is safe because monad_vm_runtime_mul (0x44e160 to 0x44e1f6) uses only rax, rcx, rdx, r8 to r13, saves r12 and r13, and has no vector instruction. The emitted code does not move rsp around the call; udiv, umod, mulmod and udivrem<4,4> realign their own frames with and rsp,-32 before their vmovdqa stores, and mul uses no stack, so the native frame's alignment cannot change a result. The result pointer equals an argument pointer at 14 sites (for example 0x5920 rdi = rsi, 0x5901 rdi = rdx, 0x51de rdi = rcx, the modulus); mul reads every limb of an operand before writing that limb, and the other helpers copy their operands first, and the runs at those sites and 27,000 aliased standalone helper runs agree with Python.

cleared.check: Task 3. The runtime helpers interpreted from the package text in the x86 model: monad_vm_runtime_mul 0x44e160, runtime::udiv 0x397250, runtime::umod 0x397710, runtime::mulmod 0x398a70, and what they call, udivrem<4,4> 0x2125b0, udivrem<8,4> 0x398560, monad::mulmod 0x3988b0 and knuth_div 0x212400. 12,000 operand sets per helper (seed 3233): the 27 by 27 grid of edge words (0, 1, 2, 3, 2^64, 2^128, 2^192, 2^255 and neighbours, 2^96, 2^160, 1e6, MIN_SQRT_PRICE, MAX_SQRT_PRICE), FullMath products of 128 to 256 bit words, SqrtPriceMath shapes (liquidity << 96 with 160-bit prices), SwapMath fee shapes, products just below and above 2^256, and denominators and moduli with a top limb of 0, 1, all ones and 2^63. Each helper also ran with the result pointer equal to each argument pointer (6,000 to 9,000 cases). Results were compared with Python integers.
cleared.result: 48,000 standalone cases and 27,000 aliased cases, 0 mismatches, 0 stops (research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/helpers.json). The helpers use BMI2 mulx (23), shlx and shrx, LZCNT, the 64-bit div (7), shld and shrd, and AVX2 vinserti128, vpinsrq, vmovq, vmovdqa, vmovdqu, vpxor and vzeroupper; none uses ADX adcx or adox. The model needed no new instruction for them (vshufps and indirect branches were added for the emitter only). Instruction coverage: mul 44 of 45, udiv and umod 35 of 39, mulmod 37 of 41, udivrem<4,4> 153 of 170, udivrem<8,4> 170 of 187, monad::mulmod 109 of 112, knuth_div 122 of 127; the lines not reached are assertion and stack-protector exits. Two planted faults in monad_vm_runtime_mul are caught: adc to add at 0x44e198 (200 of 2,000 cases differ) and the top-limb add at 0x44e1e3 dropped (842 of 2,000).

cleared.check: Task 4. The other emit kinds of the 128 un-entered value blocks, with the same driver (TASK4=1): Emitter::add 0x378260, sub 0x378da0, lt 0x37ad10, gt 0x37ae80, eq 0x385860, iszero 0x36eaa0, and_ 0x387980, or_ 0x3867c0, xor_ 0x386010, sgt 0x37a5a0 and slt 0x37a430, with 56 std::function handlers and general_bin_instr visitors reached through pointers added from the same text. Comparison results are deferred comparisons: their word is the Comparison of the final flags, and an input deferred comparison gets the 0 or 1 that random initial flags mean. Stack::alloc_literal 0x3ad360 ran from the package for SGT, and btc was added to the model for SLT.
cleared.result: 270 sites over 87 blocks (ADD 103, AND 81, SUB 33, ISZERO 24, OR 9, EQ 8, GT 5, LT 4, XOR 1, SGT 1, SLT 1; NOT has no site in these blocks): every stream equals the clang listing up to renaming (6 with a limb table read from the listing, and asmjit's -N immediates read as their 64-bit two's complement), every post-call Stack equals the next clang state including the deferred comparison slot and code, and 540,000 runs gave no wrong word (research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/realother.json, realother-SGT_SLT.json). cleared.check: Task 5. Whether the checks can fail. One-instruction faults planted in the package text (research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/scripts/faults32.json, helpers.py HFAULTS): gen1-not-spilled-before-call (Stack::spill_all_caller_save_general_regs starts at the third row, 0x3aca27), avx-not-spilled-before-udiv (spill_avx 0 at 0x383a9e), helper-args-swapped (mov_arg's rsi and rdx targets exchanged at 0x36a0a8 and 0x36a0b8), result-slot-wrong (result pointer 16k instead of 32k at 0x37f0d3), arg-slot-wrong (argument displacement 64k at 0x37ee57), free-offset-stale (StackElem::free_stack_offset reads the reserve count, 0x3ab3a3), deferred-comparison-not-negated (CSWTCH lookup dropped at 0x36b890), high-limb-dropped-in-mul-helper (0x44e1e3), and for Task 4 discharge-setcc-wrong-flag (setcc table index plus one at 0x36b6aa). cleared.result: Every plant is caught: gen1-not-spilled-before-call 6 sites (0 wrong results, 193 overwritten live words); avx-not-spilled-before-udiv 8 sites (0 wrong results, 463 overwritten live words); helper-args-swapped 10 sites (1537 wrong results, 0 overwritten live words); result-slot-wrong 22 sites (3934 wrong results, 1304 overwritten live words); arg-slot-wrong 30 sites (5307 wrong results, 0 overwritten live words); free-offset-stale 22 sites (0 wrong results, 0 overwritten live words); deferred-comparison-not-negated 1 sites (0 wrong results, 200 overwritten live words); high-limb-dropped-in-mul-helper 17 sites (1590 wrong results, 0 overwritten live words); discharge-setcc-wrong-flag 7 sites (220 wrong results, 100 overwritten live words). The unsaved general register and unsaved AVX register plants are caught by live words overwritten by the helper's own clobbers and by the stream and state comparisons, which shows that sites with live caller-saved words before the call exist and that the shipped code spills them.

cleared.check: Whether the gcc-built native emitter and its runtime helpers apply outside Monad.
cleared.result: They do not. The emitter, its virtual stack, the runtime helpers and the gcc 15.2.0 validator build are Monad's own (monad 0.16.7). The other 20 networks run interpreters (go-ethereum family, revm family, Nitro, Tempo, mega-evm and the HyperEVM node) that earlier cycles tested and that this unit does not touch. The answer for those 20 is no, on the evidence of networks.json and OPCODES.md.

leads.question: Run the package's gcc 15.2.0 emit functions on the logged real states for the 473 sites of the 128 un-entered value blocks that have still not run: MSTORE 150, MLOAD 58, KECCAK256 45, CALLER 29, SLOAD 23, SSTORE 14, SIGNEXTEND with a literal index 10, CALLDATALOAD 5, TLOAD 4, LOG2 to LOG4 6, RETURNDATASIZE 1, and the 128 terminators (JUMPI with a deferred comparison, JUMP, RETURN, REVERT and write_to_final_stack_offsets), using research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/scripts/realarith.py as the driver.
leads.why: Every value-computing arithmetic, comparison and bit site of these blocks now matches the clang harness and pyevm.py, including all of FullMath.mulDiv's blocks except their terminators. The memory, storage, hashing and terminator emitters call further runtime routines (keccak, sload, sstore, memory expansion) whose argument passing and live-register handling have not been run from the package on real states. The per-block list is research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/coverage.json.

leadResults.answer: The package's gcc 15.2.0 emitter ran whole on the real compile-time states of all 33 MUL, DIV, MOD and MULMOD sites of the 128 un-entered value blocks, the six FullMath.mulDiv blocks first, and on 270 ADD, SUB, LT, GT, EQ, ISZERO, AND, OR, XOR, SGT and SLT sites. Every stream equals the clang listing up to renaming, every post-call Stack equals the clang state, and 606,000 runs with the package's own helpers serving the calls match pyevm.py. The four runtime helpers match Python on 48,000 cases and 27,000 aliased cases. Caller-saved general registers are spilled before every call, AVX registers before udiv, umod and mulmod, and mul keeps AVX words live because its helper uses no vector register. Nine planted faults are caught. No word differs, so no swap or liquidity change by an ordinary account gains or locks anything through these blocks on Monad, and the question does not arise on the other 20 networks. The memory, storage, hashing, log and terminator sites are left as a new low-priority lead.
